newsitem.title: JORDAN: ArabBank pushes Amman index to new heights.
newsitem.headline: ArabBank pushes Amman index to new heights.

text.p: Shares in Arab Bank rose strongly in busy trade on Saturday, driving the official Amman stock exchange index to fresh three-year highs.
Arab Bank stock climbed 10 dinars on Saturday to close at 296 dinars ($417 dinars) after accounting for nearly two-thirds of turnover on the Amman bourse.
Brokers continue to attribute the bank's popularity to forecasts of strong 1997 profits, expectations of a bonus share offering, and government plans to scrap foreign share ownership ceilings.
Its shares have now gained 12 percent in the last 10 days.
"They are expecting the approval to scrap the ownership ceilings very soon," analyst Mohammad Abdallah said. "When it is approved, the shares will go above 300 dinars."
Shares in the bank have almost single-handedly pushed the official 60-share Amman Financial Market (AFM) index to its highest level since March 1994.
The index gained 1.41 percent to 167.74 points on Saturday in trade worth 1.38 million dinars.

Arab Bank shares are at a five-year high and the market's official index -- highly sensitive to moves in the price of the stock which accounts for almost one third of the Amman bourse's 3.4 billion dinar capitalisation -- has matched their gains.
Other indices, less heavily weighted in favour of the bank, paint a less rosy picture of the market's health.

The private Pearl Index of the 45 best-performing shares in terms of turnover and financial performance, gained 0.85 percent on Saturday to 81.39 points. It is still 2.40 percent down from the start of the year.
But brokers said Saturday's trade was healthy, with 15 shares rising and just nine falling.
Jordan Islamic Bank, another stock expected to benefit from the lifting of foreign ownership ceilings, rose 0.11 dinars to 3.91 dinars in trade worth 218,000 dinars. $1 = 0.709 dinars
